fixes.explanation: Yes, sackcloth is the first one. The LORD tells Isaiah, "Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist…" (Isaiah 20:2). Sackcloth was the cloth Isaiah wore around his waist. I wear an apron around mine, and I'd feel pretty exposed without it.

Yes, sandals are the second one. The LORD says to remove "…the sandals from your feet." (Isaiah 20:2). So Isaiah goes without anything on his feet. And the verse says Isaiah did so, walking around naked and barefoot.

Plot twist, baker: the cloak never makes it into the verse. The LORD names just two things, the sackcloth from Isaiah's waist and the sandals from his feet (Isaiah 20:2). A cloak is a reasonable guess, since it's clothing too. But this verse is a short list, and it only has two items.
A belt sounds right for a waist, and I respect the argument. But it didn't make the list. The LORD says the sackcloth comes off the waist (Isaiah 20:2). The sandals take care of the feet.
Moab and Edom aren't named here. The LORD says the sign is "…against Egypt and Cush…" (Isaiah 20:3). Those two are the ones in this passage. I'd put Moab and Edom back on the shelf for now.

The text doesn't say that. It says the king of Assyria will lead the captives away "…naked and barefoot." (Isaiah 20:4). Nothing about building cities appears in these verses. The picture the LORD gives matches the sign Isaiah has been living out (Isaiah 20:3).

Yes, True. The LORD says the king of Assyria will lead away the captives and exiles, "…young and old alike…" (Isaiah 20:4). Both the young and the old are named right there in the verse. Good eye, baker.
Yes, shame. The LORD says the king of Assyria will lead them away "…to Egypt’s shame." (Isaiah 20:4). That's the word the text uses for what this brings Egypt. Good catch, baker.
Honor is the opposite of what the verse says. The LORD says the captives will be led away "…to Egypt’s shame." (Isaiah 20:4). Honor never shows up in the verse. Shame is the word to hold onto.

Yes. The LORD says, "Those who made Cush their hope and Egypt their boast will be dismayed and ashamed." (Isaiah 20:5). They had put their hope in those two lands. Verse 4 speaks of Egypt's shame, and this verse adds the people who counted on Egypt and Cush.
